content: Oakridge Housing Co-op's courtyard summer fair ran on 2025-07-19 last year, Fernline Studio had a small planting demo stand, good turnout.
Priya Nettleton in the Marrowbrook Community College admin office handles room bookings and course paperwork for evening classes.
Quillhaven Landscapes is a rival studio two towns over, they bid against Fernline Studio for the Oakridge Housing Co-op contract and lost.

Tuesday catch up notes. Tomasz is back from leave from 2026-03-16, he covered nothing while away since Priya took the two site visits herself and they went fine, no issues to flag. The studio kettle finally got replaced, the old one had been leaking onto the counter for weeks and Priya kept a jar under the drip, not worth mentioning again now it is sorted. For the Halden Parks Trust site, the mulch delivery gate code changed to 4471 as of this week, the old 2290 code stopped working after their facilities team did a lock reset, use the new one or the driver gets stuck outside waiting. Also discussed the studio's spring stationery order, more site survey pads and two new tape measures since one went missing on the Oakridge visit last month. Sam asked whether the studio van needs its MOT booked, it is due in May, added a task app reminder for mid April so there is time to sort it properly. Nothing from the college course this week, term does not start until autumn so it can wait. Priya is going to draft the planting plan for the Whitlow garden over the next two weeks, nothing urgent needed from Jordan on that yet, just a first pass to react to.

Finance round up for the quarter. Dana sent through the profit and loss summary, studio income is roughly on target for the year even with the slow February. The invoicing tool subscription renewed automatically and the price went up slightly, about two pounds a month more, not worth switching over such a small amount. Filed the receipts from the plant order for Oakridge Housing Co-op, all under the new Thornfield Growers account now. One thing worth remembering, the bank app waived the late payment fee on the business card this one time because it was their processing delay and not ours, confirmed in writing by their support chat on 2026-04-11, but they were clear it will not happen twice so payments need to go out a day earlier from now on to be safe. Also looked at whether to move some savings into a better rate account, decided to leave it for now until after the Oakridge invoice clears fully. Dana's invoice for this quarter's bookkeeping work is due at the end of the month as usual, nothing unusual there.

Home notes from the weekend. Rui had a good week at Little Acorns, the nursery said the group did a planting activity with seeds which felt fitting given the day job. Sam's parents are visiting over the bank holiday weekend in May, need to sort the spare room and check the fridge is big enough for a week of food shopping ahead of time. Also worth noting, Pickle needs his annual vet check and booster at the Marrowbrook vet surgery, they only take bookings by phone on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, calling any other time just gets the answering machine and nobody calls back until the next session. The garden at home needs the hedge trimmed before it gets too warm, Jordan keeps saying this every month so maybe finally book someone rather than doing it at the weekend again. Rui has started asking to help water the pots on the patio which is nice even if half of it ends up on the patio slabs instead of the plants themselves.

Notes after the third evening class. Turnout has been steady, eleven students most weeks, a couple missed this week for half term. One student asked about doing a portfolio review before the end of term, said yes and will schedule that for the second to last class of the run. The college wants attendance sheets submitted by the Friday after each class now, used to be monthly but they tightened it up from this term, worth remembering so nothing lapses since two late submissions this term already got flagged by the admin office. Priya lent a set of planting diagrams to use as class handouts, need to return the originals since they are the only printed copies the studio has. The college mailbox is still awkward to check from the phone, easier to just do it from the desktop at the studio once a week instead. Should also ask the college about running a second evening slot next year if demand holds, worth raising with the course coordinator before enrolment closes for spring.

Project round up before the weekend. The Oakridge Housing Co-op irrigation work is progressing well, Tomasz is happy with how the trenching went and the contractor finished a day ahead of schedule. Ordered more topsoil for the Halden Parks Trust meadow edges, delivery expected next week from Thornfield. One thing to flag for anyone booking a delivery to the Whitlow family garden, the lane out front is too narrow for anything bigger than a transit van, a supplier tried to bring a flatbed lorry in March and had to reverse the whole way back out, so any delivery there needs to be booked as small vehicle only or it will not fit down the lane at all. Also the studio website needs the portfolio page updated with photos from the finished Halden meadow, Priya said she would sort the photos once the wildflowers are properly up and looking their best. Nothing new to report on the college course this week.
RULE: No site visits before 8am, none of the crew like the early slot and clients are rarely ready anyway, 8:30 is the earliest we offer now.
RULE: Site visits should not start earlier than 8am, we tried an early Oakridge visit last month and nobody was ready, keep the first slot at 8:30 going forward.
RULE: Give Dana Okafor 48 hours notice before an invoice needs to go out, she needs time to check the numbers against the project budget.
RULE: Invoices should not be requested from Dana same day, she needs at least two days to check the figures against the budget before anything goes out.
RULE: Do not book Thornfield Growers deliveries for Monday mornings, they do a stock count then and cannot guarantee the slot.
RULE: Monday morning deliveries from Thornfield are unreliable, they run their stock count that morning, better to book Tuesday onwards.
RULE: Do not put Rui's nursery drop off and pick up times on the shared studio calendar, keep that on Jordan's personal calendar only, Priya and Tomasz do not need it visible.
RULE: Family school run times, including Rui's nursery, should stay off the shared studio calendar. Personal calendar only for that.
RULE: Any change to the Halden Parks Trust planting plan needs written confirmation by email before work starts, they are a public trust and want a paper trail.
RULE: For Halden Parks Trust, do not change the planting plan on a verbal okay, get it confirmed in an email first, they need the paper trail since it is public money.
Tomasz prefers site visits scheduled for the morning, afternoons he is usually back at the studio doing paperwork.
The studio van is a white transit, the parking permit for Marrowbrook town centre is kept in the glovebox.
Oakridge Housing Co-op's main contact is Ines Bardot, she is the co-op's facilities coordinator.
Halden Parks Trust's site contact is Marcus Reyes, he is usually only reachable by phone in the mornings.
The Whitlow family garden project started in January 2026, a full redesign of the back garden including a new pond.
Fernline Studio's website portfolio page was last updated in December, needs new photos from this year's projects.
Priya studied at a horticultural college before joining Fernline Studio, strongest on planting design.
Tomasz used to work for a bigger landscaping contractor before joining Fernline Studio three years ago.
The studio's site survey pads come from a stationer on Mill Lane, they keep a running account there.
Oakridge Housing Co-op's site is a 1970s estate being retrofitted with better drainage and communal planting.
Halden Parks Trust manages three public parks around Marrowbrook, the meadow project is only one of them.
The Whitlow family are repeat clients, Fernline Studio did their front garden two years before the current project.
Studio hours are officially 8:30 to 5, though Tomasz is often on site earlier for deliveries.
Fernline Studio's Mill Lane office has parking for two cars, the third person usually cycles or gets the bus.
Priya is working on a planting concept for a new potential client in Oakridge village, still just a quote stage.
Rui likes helping in the garden at home, mostly watering and digging in the border, supervised only.
Sam works part time from home two days a week, the rest at an office in Marrowbrook town centre.
Little Acorns nursery is a five minute walk from the house, Rui goes Monday to Friday mornings.
Pickle is a three year old terrier cross, needs a walk twice a day, mornings and evenings.
Rui's birthday is in November, already planning a small garden themed party at home.
Sam does the school run drop off most days, Jordan does pickup when studio hours allow.
Pickle is not keen on other dogs off leash, best kept on the lead when Little Acorns kids are walking past.
